title: Listening practice: A request, a book talk and a price comparison
description: Three recordings: a student asks her teacher for more time, a student argues about a character's choice, and three speakers compare prices.

stimuli.title: Listen: A student talks with her teacher

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Mr. Tanaka, may I ask you something about the poster project? It's due Friday, but I'd like to turn it in on Monday instead.

turns.speaker: Mr. Tanaka
turns.text: That's three extra days. Can you tell me why?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I have two reasons. First, the library computers were down on Tuesday and Wednesday, so I lost two days of research. Second, my partner has been absent all week, which means I'm doing both parts. I've finished the research and the draft, but the poster itself still needs time.

turns.speaker: Mr. Tanaka
turns.text: Those are fair reasons. However, presentations begin Monday during first period, so I need the posters before then. Could you bring it in Monday morning before class and present last?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yes. I can come at seven forty-five, and I'll present last so the schedule doesn't change.

turns.speaker: Mr. Tanaka
turns.text: Okay, that works. But please send me your finished research notes by Friday so I know you're on track.

stimuli.title: Listen: A book talk

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: I want to argue that Tomás made the right decision in the novel The Last Ferry, even though his choice cost him something. Early in the book, Tomás finds a wallet on the dock, and he's tempted to keep the money because his family is struggling. Even so, he returns it to its owner, an elderly ferry worker. Some people in my group said he was foolish because he received no reward on the spot. I disagree, and here's my evidence. First, the ferry worker later recommends Tomás for a summer job, and that's how he gets hired. Second, on page ninety, Tomás says he could not have looked his sister in the eye if he'd kept the money. That shows his decision came from his values, not from hoping for a reward. For these reasons, I believe returning the wallet was right, because it led to a good result and because it matched the person Tomás wanted to be.

For these reasons, I believe returning the wallet was right, because it led to a good result and because it matched the person Tomás wanted to be.

stimuli.title: Listen: A class discussion about prices

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: A store sells six notebooks for nine dollars, or ten notebooks for fourteen dollars. Kofi, Lena, which is the better buy?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: I say six for nine dollars. It costs less money, and nine is smaller than fourteen.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: But Kofi, you're not buying the same number of notebooks. We have to compare the price of one notebook. Nine divided by six is one dollar fifty. Fourteen divided by ten is one dollar forty.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Oh, so one notebook costs less in the bigger pack?

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: Right. It's ten cents less for each notebook. So the ten-notebook pack is the better buy, even though the total is higher.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Kofi, does Lena's argument change your answer?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Yes. I only compared the totals, and that wasn't fair.

Nine divided by six is one dollar fifty. Fourteen divided by ten is one dollar forty. Kofi: Oh, so one notebook costs less in the bigger pack? Lena: Right. It's ten cents less for each notebook. So the ten-notebook pack is the better buy, even though the total is higher. Teacher: Kofi, does Lena's argument change your answer? Kofi: Yes. I only compared the totals, and that wasn't fair.

options.text: To switch to a different project partner.
To turn in her poster on Monday, not Friday.
To present the poster first on Monday.
To skip the class presentation entirely.

distractors.a: She says her partner is absent, but she does not ask for a different partner.
distractors.c: Priya offers to present last, not first.
distractors.d: Priya agrees to present on Monday, and she offers to present last.

items.explanation: Priya says the project is due Friday and asks to turn it in on Monday instead.

support.clue: Listen to Priya's first two sentences. Notice the words due and instead.
support.frame: Priya wants to turn in ______ on ______ instead of ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "Marco asked to take the quiz on Wednesday instead of Tuesday." The speaker names what and when. Listen for what and when in Priya's request.

misconceptions.a: mixes up a reason with the request

items.stem: Which two reasons does Priya give for her request?

options.text: The library computers were down.
Presentations start on Monday morning.
Her partner was absent all week.
She had not finished the research.

distractors.b: That is Mr. Tanaka's reason for needing the poster early, not Priya's reason.
distractors.d: Priya says she has finished the research and the draft.

items.explanation: Priya says the library computers were down and her partner has been absent all week.

support.clue: Listen for First and Second. Priya gives her reasons after those words. One choice is a reason from a different speaker.
support.frame: Priya gives two reasons: first, ______, and second, ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "I want a longer recess for two reasons. First, we sit for six hours. Second, outdoor play helps us focus." Listen for the number words that mark each reason. Find Priya's two reasons the same way.

items.stem: Why does Mr. Tanaka want the poster on Monday morning?

options.text: He needs time to grade it before lunch.
The library computers will be fixed by then.
Her partner returns to class that day.
The class presentations begin that morning.

distractors.a: Mr. Tanaka does not mention grading.
distractors.b: The library computers are mentioned only as a reason Priya lost two days of research.
distractors.c: Her partner has been absent all week; no return is mentioned.

items.explanation: Mr. Tanaka says presentations begin Monday during first period, so he needs the posters before then.

support.clue: Listen to Mr. Tanaka's reply that starts with However. His reason comes right after.
support.frame: Mr. Tanaka wants the posters on Monday morning because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "The bakery needs your order by noon because the cakes take three hours to bake." A deadline is explained by a later event. Say Mr. Tanaka's reason the same way.

items.stem: What is the speaker's main claim?

options.text: Tomás made the right choice by returning the wallet.
Tomás was foolish to return the wallet he found.
The novel is too sad for students to recommend.
The ferry worker should have kept the money.

distractors.b: That is what some people in her group said; the speaker disagrees.
distractors.c: The speaker never judges how sad the novel is.
distractors.d: The wallet belongs to the ferry worker, and the speaker talks about Tomás's choice.

items.explanation: Leila begins by saying she wants to argue that Tomás made the right decision, and she ends by saying returning the wallet was right.

support.clue: Listen to the speaker's first sentence. A claim often comes first, before the evidence.
support.frame: The speaker argues that ______ made ______ by ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "I want to argue that our school should plant a garden, because it would give every class a place to learn." A claim says what you believe. Find the speaker's claim in the book talk.

misconceptions.b: mixes up another view with the speaker's

items.stem: What does the ferry worker do later in the book?

options.text: He gives Tomás a reward of money.
He teaches Tomás to work on the ferry.
He recommends Tomás for a summer job.
He tells Tomás's sister about the wallet.

distractors.a: The speaker says Tomás received no reward on the spot.
distractors.b: The speaker mentions a recommendation, not training.
distractors.d: The sister appears only in Tomás's statement on page ninety.

items.explanation: The speaker says the ferry worker later recommends Tomás for a summer job, and that is how Tomás gets hired.

support.clue: Listen to the part of the evidence that begins with First. Notice the word later.
support.frame: Later in the book, the ferry worker ______ Tomás for ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "Later in the story, the librarian thanked Mina in front of the whole class." A speaker uses later to show an event that comes after the first one. Listen for what happened later to Tomás.

misconceptions.b: adds a detail that was not said

items.stem: Match each point in the book talk to when Leila makes it.

left.text: Tomás is tempted to keep the wallet
Tomás could not look his sister in the eye

items.explanation: Leila first says Tomás is tempted to keep the wallet, next says some people call him foolish, and last uses what Tomás says about his sister.

support.clue: Listen for the words Early in the book, Some people, and Second. They show which point comes when.
support.frame: Leila says ______ first, then ______, and last ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'First, the coach explained the rules. Next, the team practiced passing. Last, they played a short game.' Time words show the order of the points. Match each point in the book talk to when Leila says it.

items.stem: Why does Lena say Kofi's comparison isn't fair?

options.text: He divided the totals instead of comparing them.
He compared totals for packs of different sizes.
He chose the pack with more notebooks.
He used the wrong price for the smaller pack.

distractors.a: Kofi compared the totals; he did not divide anything.
distractors.c: Kofi chose the pack of six, which is the smaller pack.
distractors.d: The totals, nine and fourteen dollars, are correct; the method is the problem.

items.explanation: Lena says Kofi isn't buying the same number of notebooks, so comparing the totals is unfair; the price of one notebook should be compared.

support.clue: Listen to Lena's first reply to Kofi. She says what he did not compare.
support.frame: Kofi's comparison isn't fair because he compared ______, not ______.
support.model: Mentor example. "It isn't fair to say Class A collected more cans just because it has more students; we should compare cans per student." A speaker explains why a comparison fails. Say why Kofi's comparison fails.

facts: 9 ÷ 6 = 1.50 and 14 ÷ 10 = 1.40, so one notebook costs $0.10 less in the pack of ten.

misconceptions.d: blames the numbers instead of the method

items.stem: Sort each fact: which pack does it describe?

tokens.text: One notebook costs one dollar fifty
One notebook costs one dollar forty

items.explanation: Six notebooks cost nine dollars, so one costs one dollar fifty. Ten notebooks cost fourteen dollars, so one costs one dollar forty.

support.clue: Listen to the teacher's first sentence. It tells how many notebooks each price buys. Then listen to Lena's two divisions.
support.frame: The pack of ______ costs ______ in all, so one notebook costs ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'A small bag holds four apples and costs two dollars. A large bag holds eight apples and costs five dollars.' Each fact belongs to one bag. Sort the notebook facts by pack in the same way.
